segments.source: A 2023 Classic Evo Pro needs its boiler history established before its familiar 58 mm group becomes a selling point. The reviewed North American RI9380/46 was built with a coated aluminum boiler and has since been superseded by E24, so replacement history and the condition of the actual unit matter. Its mechanical switches, three-way solenoid and manual steam wand remain recognizable Classic strengths, with thermostat timing and sequential milk work still expected of the owner. A documented, appropriately priced example can be useful. An uncertain boiler record should outweigh enthusiasm for the Classic's accessory and modification ecosystem.

segments.source: The 58 mm format, nine-bar calibration and three-way solenoid provide a familiar manual brewing platform. Thermostats rather than a PID control the stock boiler. For a candidate used unit, a stable demonstrated brew routine and documented condition are more useful than an impressive extraction video with an unknown grinder.

segments.source: RI9380/46 changes between coffee and steam temperature within one boiler. Ask to see the complete brew–steam–return sequence, because a machine sold after years of use needs more than a working pump demonstration. The manual wand offers direct texture control but no automated finishing.
